title: MStargetR
text: MStargetR R package provides end--end pipeline processing targeted multiple reaction monitoring (MRM) liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry (LC-MS) data. title: MStargetR
text: batchCorrectR() function provides standalone signal drift interbatch correction operates independently qcCheckR pipeline. accepts simple data frame input, making suitable users already processed data tools wish apply batch correction tabular metabolomics dataset.

title: MStargetR
text: QCRFSC (QC-based Random Forest Signal Correction): Fits random forest model QC samples across run order. Robust non-linear drift patterns. Implemented via statTarget::shiftCor(). ComBat (Empirical Bayes Batch Correction): Uses empirical Bayes methods sva package adjust batch effects. Unlike QC-based methods , ComBat require QC samples – estimates removes batch effects using batch labels. makes suitable studies QC reference material available. ComBat can correct location (mean) scale (variance) batch effects, mean-combat_mean.= TRUE. Install sva via BiocManager::install("sva").

title: MStargetR
text: batchCorrectR returns named list containing: corrected_data – tibble structure input corrected metabolite values. correction_summary – tibble per-metabolite RSD correction. qc_rsd_before – Named numeric vector QC %RSD values correction. qc_rsd_after – Named numeric vector QC %RSD values correction. failed_qc – Character vector sample names flagged failed QC injections (signal < 10% batch median). plots – list ggplot objects (plot = TRUE). report – Logical indicating whether HTML report requested. report_path – Path rendered HTML report (report = TRUE rendering succeeds).

code: library(MStargetR)  # Prepare a synthetic input dataset my_data <- data.frame(   sample_name  = paste0("S", 1:20),   batch        = rep(c("plate1", "plate2"), each = 10),   sample_type  = rep(c("qc", "sample", "sample", "sample", "qc"), 4),   run_order    = 1:20,   metabolite_A = rnorm(20, mean = 100, sd = 15),   metabolite_B = rnorm(20, mean = 500, sd = 75) )  # Run batch correction with default settings (QCRFSC) result <- batchCorrectR(data = my_data)  # Access the corrected data corrected <- result$corrected_data head(corrected)  # View the correction summary (RSD before vs. after) result$correction_summary # ComBat correction (does not require QC samples) my_data_no_qc <- data.frame(   sample_name  = paste0("S", 1:20),   batch        = rep(c("plate1", "plate2"), each = 10),   sample_type  = rep("sample", 20),   run_order    = 1:20,   metabolite_A = rnorm(20, mean = 100, sd = 15),   metabolite_B = rnorm(20, mean = 500, sd = 75) )  result_combat <- batchCorrectR(   data   = my_data_no_qc,   method = "ComBat" )  # ComBat with mean-only correction result_combat_mean <- batchCorrectR(   data              = my_data_no_qc,   method            = "ComBat",   combat_mean.only  = TRUE )

title: Targeted MRM Mass Spectrometry Data Processing and Quality Control
text: ## Overview MStargetR provides complete, end--end pipeline processing targeted multiple reaction monitoring (MRM) liquid chromatography–mass spectrometry (LC-MS) data. takes raw vendor files input produces quality-controlled, batch-corrected concentration data ready downstream statistical analysis. package designed metabolomics researchers need reproducible, automated workflow handles multi-plate multi-method experiments. Cross-platform support achieved Docker, encapsulates vendor file conversion peak integration steps workflow runs Windows, macOS, Linux. interactive Shiny application also included users prefer graphical interface scripting. core pipeline consists three stages: (1) conversion proprietary vendor files open mzML format via ProteoWizard, (2) retention time optimisation peak picking/integration via Skyline, (3) quality control assessment batch signal drift correction. stage exposed independent function can used combined single script.

title: Targeted MRM Mass Spectrometry Data Processing and Quality Control
text: Vendor file conversion – msConvertR() converts proprietary instrument files (SCIEX .wiff, Bruker .d, Thermo .raw, Waters .raw, others) open mzML format using ProteoWizard msConvert Docker. Peak picking integration – PeakForgeR() performs QC-based retention time optimisation, peak boundary refinement, peak integration via Skyline Docker. Supports multi-method multi-plate projects. Quality control reporting – qcCheckR() performs missing value imputation, batch signal drift correction, sample feature filtering, generates HTML Excel reports interactive PCA control chart visualisations. Standalone batch correction – batchCorrectR() provides independent QC-based signal drift interbatch correction using random forest (QCRFSC) empirical Bayes (ComBat) methods. accepts simple data.frame can used outside main MStargetR pipeline. Interactive Shiny application – launchMStargetR() launches GUI running full pipeline without writing code. Transition list validation – transition_checkR() verifies MRM transitions unique, compare_mrm_template_with_guide() confirms internal standards transition list match concentration guide. Multi-method multi-plate support – pipeline functions handle projects spanning multiple analytical methods instrument plates, combining results common long-term reference samples consistent metabolite naming conventions used.

title: Standalone Interbatch Correction for Targeted LC-MS Data — batchCorrectR
text: correction pipeline proceeds follows: Input validation: Checks required columns exist, metabolite data numeric, QC samples present batch. Metabolite detection: Identifies numeric columns metadata columns metabolite features. Excluded metadata columns defined .METADATA_COLS (see R/batchCorrectR_Utils.R) include sample_name, batch, sample_type, run_order, sample_plate_id, sample_timestamp, sample_matrix, synthetic_qc, others. Row filtering: sample_tags supplied, rows whose sample_type match qc_label provided tags dropped correction. step runs QC flagging affects correction model returned corrected_data. QC flagging: Flags QC injections total signal less 10 percent batch median, reclassifying regular samples prevent distorting correction model. File preparation: Creates PhenoFile.csv ProfileFile.csv format required statTarget::shiftCor, ensuring QC samples bookend batch. Signal correction: Runs statTarget::shiftCor specified method model remove systematic signal drift. Post-correction adjustment: Adjusts corrected values QC means match original pre-correction scale, preserving biological interpretation absolute values. Reporting: Optionally generates /RSD comparison tables visualisations including run-order plots PCA. QCRFSC (QC-based Random Forest Signal Correction) fits random forest model QC samples across run order applies learned correction samples. robust non-linear drift patterns.

Must specific column names. See examples structure mrm_template_list. Must include mrm_guide labelled "SIL_guide" associated concentration guide labelled "conc_guide". Can contain multiple combinations stored separate lists, see examples. QC_sample_label character string containing key tags filter QC samples file names.  E.g. "qc". sample_tags character vector specifying tags filter sample types file names. E.g. c("sample","control", "qc"). mv_threshold numeric value  0 100 specifying threshold missing values data. Default 50(50%). batch_method Character string specifying batch correction method. One "QCRFSC" (random forest, default) "ComBat" (empirical Bayes, QC-free). batch_ntree Integer. Number trees random forest method. Default 500. Ignored batch_method "QCRFSC". batch_coCV Numeric. Coefficient variation cutoff (percentage, 1–100) feature filtering inside statTarget. Features QC CV threshold removed. Default 100 (effectively filtering). batch_Frule Numeric. Filtering rule (0-1) missing values inside statTarget. Default 0 (filtering). batch_imputeM Character string. Imputation method missing values. One "minHalf" (default), "median", "mean", "knn". combat_par.prior Logical. TRUE (default), use parametric empirical Bayes adjustments. used batch_method = "ComBat". combat_mean.Logical. TRUE, correct mean batch effect. Default FALSE. used batch_method = "ComBat". combat_ref.batch Optional character string specifying reference batch. Default NULL. used batch_method = "ComBat". Must match value column selected batch_column (sample_plate_id batch_column NULL). batch_column Optional character. Name column imputed concentration data holds batch identifier used ComBat. NULL (default) canonical sample_plate_id column used. Set drive correction arbitrary user-named column (e.g. plate, run_batch); chosen column's values become valid choices combat_ref.batch. used batch_method = "ComBat". write_rda Logical. TRUE (default) master_list RDA file written synchronously final step pipeline. Set FALSE caller intends write RDA --band — example, Shiny GUI passes FALSE can surface results user immediately fire separate background job calls export_master_list_rda returned master_list. XLSX HTML exports unaffected. rda_compress Compression option forwarded save. Default FALSE (compression). R's single-threaded gzip pass serialized master_list can take hours ~50+ plate cohorts producing apparent hang 54-plate run, default accept 5-10x larger .rda disk exchange save completes seconds--minutes. Pass "gzip", "bzip2", "xz" opt compression archival runs. date_order Controls AcquiredTime column PeakForgeR reports (Skyline exports OS locale whoever ran export) parsed. One "auto" (default; pipeline inspects cohort, prefers mzML startTimeStamp ISO 8601 headers available, chooses unambiguous order cohort's parse pattern _YYYYMMDD$ plate-name hints), "dmy" (day-first slash/dash formats), "mdy" (month-first slash/dash formats), "ymd" / "iso" (ISO 8601 ).
